To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Financial incentives induce more reviews, but not necessarily longer ones, 2) Social norms induce longer reviews, but not more of them, and 3) Combining financial incentives with social norms induces the largest volumes of the longest reviews.

(a) financial incentives are more successful at stimulating review volume, whereas social norms are more successful at inducing longer reviews; (b) the combination of financial incentive and social norms outperforms either incentive alone in terms of review volume; (c) social norms outperform financial incentives in terms of review length, and (d) the combination of both incentives is the most effective at inducing longer reviews.

1) financial incentives are more efficient in stimulating the volume of reviews, whereas social norms are more efficient at stimulating the length of reviews, 2) the combination of financial and social norms yields better results than either treatment alone, and 3) the effectiveness of the combined treatment is driven by its effect on the length rather than the volume of reviews.
